bug_semantics: IPX filesystem storage decides whether a requested image id stays inside the configured dir(s) with a raw string prefix check: join/resolve(dir, id) then filePath.startsWith(dir) without a trailing path separator. When dir is a resolved path such as /cwd/public, an id of ../public123/test.png (normalized by ipx withLeadingSlash to /../public123/test.png) becomes /cwd/public123/test.png via path/pathe join, which still startsWith('/cwd/public') and is served. The GHSA PoC contrasts that with ../publi123/test.png, which fails the prefix test. CWE-22 path traversal; library and HTTP callers can read images from a sibling directory that shares the allowed prefix. Affected npm ipx ranges are <1.3.2, >=2.0.0-0 <2.1.1, and >=3.0.0 <3.1.1.
flaw_origin: On 2021-02-03 the human rewrite a60fb0d44b96c9f135af3295730c3da13fbc3e6c ('feat!: rewrite ipx') replaced the pre-rewrite FSAdapter confinement relative(dir, resolved).includes('..') in src/input/fs.ts with a new src/source/filesystem.ts check !isValidPath(id) || id.includes('..') || !fsPath.startsWith(rootDir). That startsWith(rootDir) primitive is the advisory mechanism. The extra id.includes('..') filter was later dropped in ec5c15d2ecfa3a5c9c550b918f84cf2f87085f90 while keeping the same prefix test, after which the GHSA ../public123 PoC works even without an absolute id. Later storage/multi-dir refactors only renamed variables and files; they did not first-write the comparison. The 2025-07-24 #271 patches append '/' to the prefix on v1/v2/v3.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2025-54387 / GHSA-mm3p-j368-7jcr is a published, non-withdrawn CWE-22 in unjs/ipx. Filesystem storage builds a candidate path with join/resolve against the configured dir and then uses String.startsWith on that dir without a trailing separator, so a sibling directory whose absolute path is a string prefix of the allowlist (./public vs ../public123) is treated as in-bounds. The GHSA PoC and the #271 regression test are that exact bypass. The 2025-07-24 fix is the one-character semantic change startsWith(dir) -> startsWith(dir + '/'), landed on main as 81693ddbfc062cc922e4e2406e8427ab4e3ad214 (advisory-cited; also v3.1.1) and cherry-picked to v2 (81b86b14ac77f58f89602112309cad2cb3d8c16c / v2.1.1) and v1 (94627ef55161ab8ea62956bbd71700a77643c03a / v1.3.2). BIC: git log -L / -S show the confinement primitive !fsPath.startsWith(rootDir) is first written in a60fb0d44b96c9f135af3295730c3da13fbc3e6c when the 2021 rewrite replaced a correct path.relative(..)-based check. Parent 11d1e1aa86350a9f095a175844a09a0f9a6b598b is present and the startsWith(dir) check is absent there, so this is a first-write, not a move. The rewrite is a single-parent direct commit with no reconstructable public members, so it is not discarded as a squash aggregate. Subsequent storage rewrite (#164) and multi-dir support (#203) only relocate/rename the same comparison and are not BICs. ec5c15d2 (issue #56, drop is-valid-path / id.includes('..')) made the documented ../public123 PoC succeed but did not first-write the flawed prefix test; the advisory and the actual patch target startsWith, and even the original form was already prefix-bypassable via an absolute id that shares the dir prefix without containing '..'. AI second, BIC-only: a60fb0d is authored and committed by human maintainer Pooya Parsa (pi0) in February 2021 with empty trailers and no bot identity, so the verdict is NOT_AI.
